relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: The release of CGRP occurs following the activation of TRPV1 and TRPA1 receptors [21,22].

relationships.subject: NGF
relationships.evidence_quote: Nerve growth factor (NGF) is involved in the growth and function of sensory nerves and appears to play an important role in increasing CGRP production in dorsal root ganglia [15].

relationships.subject: CGRP1 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: The binding of CGRP to the CGRP1 receptor results in increased intracellular cAMP levels, activation of protein kinase A, and the opening of ATP-sensitive K+ channels [26].

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: This effect may be associated with CGRP’s ability to stimulate vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), promoting neovascularization in the injured area.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: It appears to inhibit gastric acid secretion and gastric motility [81].

key_findings: Review: CGRP regulates vasodilation, inflammation, GI motility and metabolism beyond nociception, with context-dependent pro- and anti-inflammatory roles
CGRP release follows TRPV1/TRPA1 activation; CGRP antagonists have mainly GI side effects and minimal vascular effects
